tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kits
tips.text: To strip old paint from kits, use Mr. Hobby Super Thinner (Toluene) or Acetone. Apply sparingly on a cotton swab, gently rub painted areas. For stubborn paint, use Acetone with a soft brush, rinse with water, and dry thoroughly before painting. Always wear gloves and work in a well-ventilated area.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To repair broken photo-etched parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue like Tamiya Extra Thin Cement. Apply a small amount to the joining edge, press parts together immediately. Use tweezers or clamps to hold them in place until set. Sand any excess glue with fine grit sandpaper.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog an Iwata airbrush, disassemble it and soak the nozzle and needle in Acetone for 15 minutes. Use a soft brush to scrub gently, then reassemble and test-spray with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner. If clog persists, repeat process or consult manufacturer's cleaning kit.

tips.title: Fixing Warped Parts
tips.text: To repair warped plastic parts, place the piece between two flat surfaces, then gently heat with a hairdryer on low setting. As it warms, carefully apply pressure to straighten it. Once flattened, allow it to cool completely while held in place. For severe warping, use a heat gun and clamp.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: To prevent frost from forming on rattle cans, warm them gently in warm water (not hot) for 5-10 minutes before use. Shake vigorously to mix paint thoroughly. Apply paint in well-ventilated areas and avoid painting in cold, damp conditions. Always test spray first on scrap material.
